title: PAH-OMC-020 diagonal obstruction to fixed-volume all-power locality
question: Can the R-562 fixed-k locality threshold provide one fixed finite n beyond the locality frontier for every generator power k?
finding: No. For every nonconstant finite-support maximum s_f>=0 and every finite n, k=n+1 gives n<N_k(f)=max(2,s_f+2k+1). Lean proves the universal diagonal witness and no-uniform-eventuality statement. This blocks only the route that sums R-562 fixed-k identities termwise at one fixed n.
decision_reason: The proposed fixed-n all-power upgrade is exactly false by arithmetic. The result is a scoped negative boundary, not a no-go theorem for semigroup convergence: a uniform tail, cancellation estimate, common path route or form/resolvent route could still bypass it.
boundary: PAH-001, PAH-OMC-013, OMC-004, the original comparison map, Gibbs/rate normalization and external stochastic Markov time remain unchanged. No exponential series, j limit, anchored-n limit or R-512 identification is taken.
method: Re-derive the frozen OMC-013 root radius two at levels 2 through 9.
For arbitrary finite n choose the diagonal witness k=n+1 and verify n<N_k(f) for representative s_f values.
Compile Lean proofs of threshold_unbounded and no_uniform_eventual.
Run independent geometry reconstruction, hostile route-scope controls and the integrated replay.
next_action: Seek one source-authorized uniform word/factorial tail, cancellation estimate, common path-space construction or form/resolvent route that bypasses the fixed-n all-power obstruction without changing PAH-001.
revisit_condition: Reopen when such a uniform mechanism is hash-pinned or when a defect in the OMC-013 radius-two/threshold derivation is found; do not repeat the same diagonal arithmetic.
